source_neutral.procedure: Work on a scoped approval workflow represented as a set of teams, queues and handoffs. Each request follows a route from submission to approval, and ticket events are the points at which its progress is recorded. The quantities to estimate are the expected waiting contributions of individual handoffs within comparable operating conditions. The procedure assumes, subject to checking, that (a) enough requests follow routes that overlap but differ, (b) timestamps identify comparable events, and (c) a route's duration can be approximated as the sum of its handoff waits plus processing time and other explicitly represented delays. The packet does not establish that these conditions hold or that the records exist. Overall process: define scope and events; reconstruct routes from ticket histories; measure path durations; fit a model that allocates duration to handoffs; check the allocation on reserved requests and across alternative modeling choices; and, if a delay concentration survives those checks, run one bounded pilot change at that handoff with pre-specified criteria, comparison, guardrails and end point.
source_neutral.action: 1. Select a case family, an observation period, and consistent start and end events. 2. Reconstruct the routes requests actually followed, including rework, from ticket histories; use interviews to clarify what events mean and to resolve routing uncertainties. 3. Measure elapsed times over the available submission-to-approval paths and over paths between intermediate recorded events, retaining timestamp uncertainty and route uncertainty. 4. Build a candidate model that predicts each path's duration from its constituent handoff contributions plus separately represented processing or other delays. 5. Account for recorded case type, demand and staffing by stratification or by explicit model terms. 6. Compare measured and predicted durations across many overlapping routes, then iteratively adjust handoff contributions, constrained to be nonnegative, to reduce the discrepancies, applying an explicit penalty that discourages differences between contributions that the data do not support. 7. Hold back a set of requests for prediction checks, and compare results across plausible route interpretations, penalty settings and model forms. 8. Set the fit-improvement and iteration stopping rules before fitting. 9. If a delay concentration survives these checks, propose one bounded pilot at that handoff, for example assigning a named receiving owner for a defined case family. 10. Before the pilot starts, specify its duration, a comparable control or staged comparison, the smallest useful turnaround improvement, and acceptable limits for errors, workload and downstream queues. 11. Compare pilot outcomes under comparable demand and staffing; stop early and revert if a guardrail is breached, otherwise end at the specified duration.
source_neutral.observables: For the estimation stage: measured-minus-predicted durations, grouped by route and by shared handoffs; intervals between intermediate events; and queue records where available. The pattern of interest is repeated positive discrepancies on routes that share a given handoff, relative to otherwise comparable routes that bypass that handoff. Also observed: whether model revisions remove this pattern on the reserved requests, and whether the estimated concentration stays stable across plausible modeling choices (route interpretations, penalties, model forms). For the pilot stage: total turnaround, the wait at the affected handoff, downstream waits, errors and workload, each relative to the specified comparison. All of these are proposed observations; none are reported findings.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: Discrepancy patterns across routes constrain which combinations of handoff waiting contributions could account for the observed durations. Diverse overlapping routes and intermediate recorded events can help separate individual contributions; handoffs that are always traversed together may be identifiable solely as a combined delay region. Convergence of the fitting procedure by itself does not validate the inferred locations. A concentration that holds up across the prediction checks and sensitivity checks justifies prioritizing that region for inspection and for the bounded pilot; it does not establish the mechanism of the delay or that a given change is a causal remedy. A pilot that meets the predefined improvement criterion without guardrail breaches supports retaining the change within the tested case family and operating conditions, to the extent that its comparison accounts for alternative explanations. An inconclusive or unsuccessful pilot justifies withholding expansion and revisiting the proposed allocation or mechanism. Multiple allocations can fit the same path times, and a good fit cannot establish causality.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: teams, queues and handoffs making up the approval workflow; individual requests; the route each request follows from submission to approval, including rework loops; ticket events as recorded points along a route; paths, either full submission-to-approval or between intermediate recorded events; per-handoff waiting contributions (nonnegative); processing time and other delays represented as separate terms; strata or model terms for case type, demand and staffing; a reserved subset of requests for prediction checks; a set of alternative route interpretations, penalty settings and model forms; and, for the pilot, the affected handoff, the defined case family, the control or staged comparison, the outcome measures and the guardrail measures. Relationships: each path's duration is modeled as the sum of the contributions of the handoffs it contains plus the separately represented delays; routes overlap by sharing some handoffs and differ in others, and this overlap pattern is what allows contributions to be separated; handoffs that always occur together on the same routes are treated as one combined delay region; estimates are conditional on comparable operating conditions; the pilot is conditional on a concentration surviving the prediction and sensitivity checks, and pilot conclusions are conditional on comparability of demand and staffing between pilot and comparison.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Specified follow-ups: (1) Where coverage cannot distinguish adjacent handoffs, seek intermediate timestamps or additional naturally occurring routes before naming an individual handoff as the bottleneck. (2) Where estimates change substantially across plausible models, or discrepancies on reserved requests remain structured, revise the model or collect the missing observations. (3) Where a concentration survives the checks, inspect that region and run the single bounded pilot at that handoff with the pre-specified duration, comparison, smallest useful improvement and guardrail limits. (4) Where the pilot is inconclusive or unsuccessful, revisit the proposed allocation of delay or the proposed mechanism. (5) Obtain further evidence before generalizing beyond the tested case family and operating conditions. No follow-up beyond these is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions the procedure depends on, none of which the packet establishes: sufficient overlapping-but-different routes, timestamps that identify comparable events, approximately additive route durations, and existence of the records. Sources of distortion in the inferred contributions: sparse or uneven route coverage; missing or inconsistent timestamps; uncertain entry events and routes; unrecorded processing; case selection; and changes in staffing or demand. Penalty choices and the additive assumption may produce apparent concentrations; congestion, parallel work and rework may violate the additive approximation. Multiple allocations can fit the same path times, and a good fit cannot establish causality. A supported concentration does not establish the delay mechanism or a causal remedy. Conditional rules: if coverage cannot distinguish adjacent handoffs, report their combined contribution and do not name an individual bottleneck until intermediate timestamps or additional naturally occurring routes are obtained; if estimates change substantially across plausible models, or reserved-request discrepancies remain structured, withhold localization; if comparable pilot conditions cannot be established, report the observed differences with that uncertainty and withhold causal attribution. Pilot conclusions apply to the tested case family and operating conditions; generalization beyond them requires further evidence. Stopping rules: fit-improvement and iteration stopping rules are set before fitting (their specific values are unspecified), and reaching convergence does not by itself validate the inferred locations; the pilot stops early and is reverted if a guardrail for errors, workload or downstream queues is breached, and otherwise ends at the pre-specified duration. All observations are proposed, not reported.
